deed: הנס קרבס, פליט יהודי מגרמניה, תיאר בשפילד את מחזור קרבס שמפיק אנרגיה בתא
title: Hans Krebs, a Jewish refugee from Germany, worked out the citric acid cycle in Sheffield and won the Nobel Prize

trailer.text: Hans Krebs, born in Hildesheim, Germany, won the Nobel Prize for the discovery of the citric acid cycle.
On 24 April 1933 Krebs wrote to Hopkins, head of the biochemistry laboratory at Cambridge, that because he was Jewish he had lost his position and all possibility to work in Germany.
Hopkins wrote to him that he absolutely wished to help him, and Krebs's co-workers packed his instruments into 16 wooden crates and shipped them to England.

In 1935 Krebs was appointed Lecturer at the University of Sheffield, and there, according to the Department of Biochemistry at Cambridge, he worked out the citric acid cycle together with William Johnson.
According to the Nobel Prize website, energy-rich molecules in this cycle were ultimately converted into ATP, which provides energy for other processes in the cell.

stations.title: From Hildesheim to Freiburg: a first cycle

paragraphs.text: Hans Adolf Krebs was born on 25 August 1900 in Hildesheim, Germany.
According to the Leopoldina record, his father, Georg Krebs, was a Jewish ear, nose and throat doctor, and his mother was Alma.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, both his parents were Jewish with no religious association, and his father was completely immersed in German culture.
According to the Leopoldina, he was a German-British physician and biochemist.
He received a doctorate at the University of Hamburg; the sources differ on the year.
In 1926 he was appointed Assistant to Professor Otto Warburg at the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Biology in Berlin-Dahlem, and he remained there until 1930.

According to ChemistryViews, after he was forced to leave Germany in 1933 and began his research in Cambridge, his work remained centered on a seemingly simple question: how do cells break down nutrients, and what intermediate products are produced?
According to the Leopoldina, Krebs habilitated in Freiburg in 1932 and, together with Kurt Henseleit, discovered the urea cycle, also called the Krebs-Henseleit cycle.

According to the Royal College of Physicians, the work on urea synthesis was the first demonstration of a metabolic cycle, and it earned him an international reputation almost immediately and led to his appointment as Privat Dozent at the University of Freiburg ‹c7›.
According to the same source, he also introduced into the tissue-slice technique a new medium simulating blood plasma, which was later widely used around the world.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, within three months of Hitler's assumption of power all academic teachers who were of the Jewish race were dismissed or placed on leave.

A letter from the Ministry of Education, quoted in ChemistryViews, stated that all members of the Jewish race employed in the civil service or educational facilities would be suspended until a further decision was made.
On 12 April 1933 Krebs was immediately suspended by the Dean of the Medical Faculty, the surgeon E. Rehn.
According to the Leopoldina, Krebs, who came from a Jewish family of doctors, was initially placed on forced leave following the 1933 law.
On 24 April he wrote to Hopkins that because he was Jewish he had lost his position and all possibility to work in Germany.
According to the Leopoldina, on 15 July 1933 the rector of the University of Freiburg informed him of his final dismissal from all university duties.
On 22 April 1933 Albert Szent-Györgyi advocated for him in Cambridge, after agreeing to give him a sample of ascorbic acid.
On 26 April Otto Warburg offered him, if he lost his position, a place as a scientific guest in Berlin, with an apartment, a study and about 250 Marks a month.

stations.title: 16 crates, 10 Marks and a bicycle for 3 pounds

paragraphs.text: On 29 April 1933 Hopkins wrote to Krebs that he admired his work so much that he absolutely wished to help him.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, Hopkins, head of the biochemistry laboratory at Cambridge and president of the Royal Society, invited Krebs to work in his laboratory.
On 24 June he offered him a Rockefeller stipend of 300 pounds a year, an amount he considered too little for a scientist like him.
According to JTA, Krebs was allowed to take only 10 Marks out of Nazi Germany, but he managed to transport much of his laboratory equipment.
In early June 1933 his co-workers packed his instruments, including two Warburg baths and 24 manometers, into 16 wooden crates and several suitcases, and shipped them to England.
On 14 June his father wrote him a farewell letter, expressing the hope that his son would receive more recognition and luck abroad than he had received in his homeland.
According to ChemistryViews, his first purchase in Cambridge was a used bicycle for 3 pounds.
According to Harnack House, he enrolled as a student again in Great Britain, this time in biochemistry.
According to the Department of Biochemistry at Cambridge, he served as a Demonstrator in the department until 1935.

stations.title: Sheffield: pigeon muscle and citric acid

paragraphs.text: In 1935 Krebs was appointed Lecturer in Pharmacology at the University of Sheffield, and in 1938 Lecturer-in-Charge of the Department of Biochemistry founded there.
According to the Department of Biochemistry at Cambridge, in Sheffield, together with William Johnson, Krebs resolved the sequence of reactions they called the citric acid cycle.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, Albert Szent-Györgyi had shown that the rate of oxidation in muscle was greatly increased by adding succinic acid or related dicarboxylic acids.

According to the Department of Biochemistry at Cambridge, Krebs and Johnson measured the decline in metabolic rate of a suspension of fresh, minced pigeon breast muscle, and found that adding a salt of citric acid extended the "life" of the sample three-fold.
According to the same source, they showed that a cyclical pathway was involved.
According to the Nobel Prize website, in 1937 Krebs was able to present a complete picture of an important part of metabolism: the citric acid cycle.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, one turn of the cycle produces two molecules of carbon dioxide and is associated with the consumption of two molecules of oxygen.

According to the same source, the cycle is responsible for the oxidation of most food to carbon dioxide and water, and it is the main oxidative pathway in most forms of life, from bacteria to mammals.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, the editor of Nature informed Krebs that, owing to congestion of papers, they could not publish his letter, and advised him to submit it elsewhere.
According to the Leopoldina, because of the rejection Krebs could only publish his work in a less prestigious journal.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, the paper was sent to the journal Enzymologia, which published it a few months after submission.
According to the same source, the formulation of the tricarboxylic acid cycle was one of the most important milestones in the development of biochemistry.

stations.title: British citizen, vitamin C and a research unit

paragraphs.text: Krebs became a British citizen a few days after the outbreak of war in 1939, and a large part of his activities in the following years was connected with the war effort.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, with the help of conscientious objectors Krebs established quantitatively the minimum amount of vitamin C required to prevent scurvy.
According to the same source, the results showed that 30 milligrams of vitamin C a day allow an ample margin of safety.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, in 1944 the Medical Research Council decided to set up a unit for research in cell metabolism at the University of Sheffield, with Krebs as its director.
According to his Nobel autobiography, in 1945 he was raised to Professor and to Director of the Council's research unit established in his department.
In 1947 he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of London.

stations.title: Nobel, knighthood and a street in Freiburg

paragraphs.text: Krebs was awarded the Nobel Prize for the discovery of the citric acid cycle.
According to the Department of Biochemistry at Cambridge, he won the 1953 Prize in Physiology or Medicine, shared with Fritz Albert Lipmann.
According to the Leopoldina, he received numerous other awards, including the Lasker Award for Basic Medical Research (1953), the Royal Medal (1954) and the Copley Medal (1961).
According to the University of Freiburg, in 1958 Queen Elizabeth II knighted him, and he received the title Sir.
According to the Leopoldina, in 1966 he became an honorary citizen of his native city of Hildesheim, and in 2012 a street in Freiburg was named after him.
In 1954 Krebs was appointed Whitley Professor of Biochemistry at the University of Oxford.

According to the Royal College of Physicians, when he consulted Rudolph Peters before the move, Peters thought that Krebs was not the ideal person for the post, and Krebs probably did not find it easy to fit into Oxford, at least at first.
According to the same source, the glyoxylate cycle, a modification of the citric acid cycle, was discovered during the Oxford period.
In 1957 he published, together with H. L. Kornberg, a survey of energy transformations in living matter.
According to the Leopoldina, he died on 22 November 1981 in Oxford, and he was scientifically active until shortly before his death.
According to JTA, he was a Jewish refugee from Germany who became one of Britain's most distinguished scientists, and he was a professor of biochemistry at Sheffield and Oxford Universities.
According to the Royal College of Physicians, Krebs trained a large number of biochemists, and his influence on the development of biochemistry, in Britain and internationally, was profound.
According to the University of Freiburg, he was one of the few German-Jewish scholars who were able to continue their careers without interruption after banishment from Nazi Germany.
In 1938 he married Margaret Cicely Fieldhouse, of Wickersley, Yorkshire.
According to the Leopoldina, his son, John Krebs, is a professor of zoology at Oxford and a member of the House of Lords.

claims.text: הנס אדולף קרבס נולד בהילדסהיים שבגרמניה ב-25 באוגוסט 1900.
claims.quote: Sir Hans Adolf Krebs was born at Hildesheim, Germany, on August 25th, 1900.

claims.text: נימוק פרס נובל לקרבס היה על גילוי מחזור חומצת הלימון.
claims.quote: for his discovery of the citric acid cycle

claims.text: במכתבו להופקינס מ-24 באפריל 1933 כתב קרבס שמפני שהוא יהודי איבד את משרתו ואת כל האפשרות לעבוד בגרמניה.
claims.quote: Because I am Jewish, I have lost not only my position, but also all possibility to work in Germany.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, סר פרדריק גאולנד הופקינס, ראש מעבדת הביוכימיה בקיימברידג' ונשיא החברה המלכותית, הזמין את קרבס לעבוד במעבדתו.
claims.quote: Sir Frederick Gowland Hopkins, who was head of the biochemistry laboratory at Cambridge, and at that time president of The Royal Society, invited Krebs to work in his laboratory.

claims.text: ב-29 באפריל 1933 כתב הופקינס לקרבס שהוא מעריך את עבודתו כל כך שהוא רוצה בהחלט לעזור לו.
claims.quote: I admire your work so much that I absolutely wish to help you.

claims.text: בתחילת יוני 1933 עמיתיו של קרבס ארזו את מכשיריו, כולל שני אמבטי ורבורג ו-24 מנומטרים, ב-16 ארגזי עץ ובמספר מזוודות ושלחו אותם לאנגליה.
claims.quote: his loyal co-workers pack his instruments, including two Warburg baths and 24 manometers, into 16 wooden crates and several suitcases and ship them to England.

claims.text: ב-1935 מונה קרבס למרצה לפרמקולוגיה באוניברסיטת שפילד, וב-1938 למרצה האחראי על המחלקה לביוכימיה שהוקמה שם.
claims.quote: In 1935, he was appointed Lecturer in Pharmacology at the University of Sheffield, and in 1938 Lecturer-in-Charge of the Department of Biochemistry then newly founded there.

claims.text: לפי המחלקה לביוכימיה בקיימברידג', בשפילד, בשיתוף פעולה עם וויליאם ג'ונסון, פענח קרבס את רצף התגובות שכינו מחזור חומצת הלימון.
claims.quote: It was there, in collaboration with William Johnson, that he resolved the sequence of reactions that they called the citric acid cycle.

claims.text: לפי אתר פרס נובל, מולקולות עתירות אנרגיה כימית במחזור הומרו בסופו של דבר ל-ATP, המספק אנרגיה כימית לתהליכים ביוכימיים אחרים בתא.
claims.quote: The latter are ultimately converted into adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which provides chemical energy to facilitate other biochemical processes in the cell.

claims.text: לפי אתר פרס נובל, ב-1937 הצליח קרבס להציג תמונה שלמה של חלק חשוב במטבוליזם, מחזור חומצת הלימון.
claims.quote: in 1937 Hans Krebs was able to present a complete picture of an important part of metabolism—the citric acid cycle.

claims.text: לפי המחלקה לביוכימיה בקיימברידג', קרבס זכה בפרס נובל לפיזיולוגיה או רפואה ב-1953 על גילוי מחזור חומצת הלימון, במשותף עם פריץ אלברט ליפמן.
claims.quote: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1953 for his discovery of the citric acid cycle, shared with Fritz Albert Lipmann.

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת פרייבורג, ב-1958 הוענק לקרבס תואר אבירות על ידי המלכה אליזבת השנייה והוא קיבל את התואר סר.
claims.quote: In 1958 Krebs was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II and received the title Sir.

claims.text: לפי רשומת הלאופולדינה, קרבס נולד לאביו היהודי ג'ורג' קרבס, רופא אף אוזן וגרון, ולאמו אלמה.
claims.quote: Hans Krebs was born to Jewish otolaryngologist Georg Krebs and his wife Alma in Hildesheim, Germany, on 25 August 1900.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, שני הוריו של קרבס היו יהודים ללא זיקה דתית, ואביו היה שקוע לחלוטין בתרבות הגרמנית.
claims.quote: Both his parents were Jewish but they had no religious association, and particularly his father was completely immersed in German culture.

claims.quote: Hans Krebs was a German-British physician and biochemist.

claims.text: לפי אוטוביוגרפיית נובל, קרבס קיבל תואר דוקטור ברפואה מאוניברסיטת המבורג ב-1925.
claims.quote: he took, in 1925, his M.D. degree at the University of Hamburg

claims.quote: In 1926 he was appointed Assistant to Professor Otto Warburg at the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Biology at Berlin-Dahlem, where he remained until 1930.

claims.text: לפי ChemistryViews, עבודתו של קרבס התמקדה בשאלה פשוטה לכאורה: כיצד תאים מפרקים חומרי מזון ואילו תוצרי ביניים נוצרים.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, סיבוב אחד של המחזור מייצר שתי מולקולות פחמן דו-חמצני ומלווה בצריכת שתי מולקולות חמצן.
claims.quote: One turn of the cycle brings about the production of two molecules of carbon dioxide associated with the consumption of two molecules of oxygen.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, המחזור אחראי לחמצון רוב המזון לפחמן דו-חמצני ומים, והוא המסלול החימצוני העיקרי ברוב צורות החיים מחיידקים ועד יונקים.
claims.quote: This cycle is responsible for the oxidation of most of our food to carbon dioxide and water, and is the main oxidative pathway in most forms of life from bacteria to mammals.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, בעורך Nature הודיע לקרבס, בגלל עומס מאמרים, שלא יוכל לפרסם את מכתבו ויעץ לו להגיש אותו למקום אחר.
claims.quote: The editor of Nature informed Krebs that, owing to congestion of papers, they could not publish his letter at the time, and advised him to submit his paper elsewhere.

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, בגלל דחיית Nature יכול היה קרבס לפרסם את עבודתו רק בכתב עת פחות יוקרתי.
claims.quote: This meant that Krebs could only publish his work in a less prestigious journal.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, המאמר נשלח לכתב העת Enzymologia, שפרסם אותו כמה חודשים לאחר ההגשה.
claims.quote: This paper, or a greatly expanded version of it, was in fact sent to the journal Enzymologia, which published it a few months after submission.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, ניסוח מחזור חומצות הטריקרבוקסיל היה אחד מאבני הדרך החשובות ביותר בהתפתחות הביוכימיה.
claims.quote: It is no exaggeration to say that the formulation of the tricarboxylic acid cycle was one of the most important milestones in the development of biochemistry.

claims.text: קרבס קיבל אזרחות בריטית ימים ספורים לאחר פרוץ המלחמה ב-1939, וחלק גדול מפעילותו בשנים שאחר כך היה קשור למאמץ המלחמתי.
claims.quote: Krebs became a British citizen a few days after the outbreak of war in 1939, and a large part of his activities during the following years was connected with the war effort.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, בעזרת סרבני מצפון קבע קרבס באופן כמותי את הכמות המינימלית של ויטמין C הנחוצה למניעת צפדינה.
claims.quote: By making use of conscientious objectors, he established quantitatively the minimum amounts of vitamin C required for the prevention of scurvy.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, תוצאות הניסויים של קרבס הראו ש-30 מיליגרם ויטמין C ביום מותירים מרווח ביטחון נרחב.
claims.quote: especially the fact that 30 milligrams of vitamin C a day allow an ample margin of safety

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, ב-1944 החליטה מועצת המחקר הרפואי להקים באוניברסיטת שפילד יחידה למחקר בחילוף חומרים תאי, בניהולו של קרבס.
claims.quote: In 1944 the Medical Research Council decided to set up a unit for research in cell metabolism at the University of Sheffield, with Krebs as its director.

claims.text: לפי אוטוביוגרפיית נובל, ב-1945 הועלה קרבס לדרגת פרופסור ולמנהל יחידת מחקר של מועצת המחקר הרפואי שהוקמה במחלקתו.
claims.quote: In 1945 this appointment was raised to that of Professor, and of Director of a Medical Research Council’s research unit established in his Department.

claims.text: קרבס נבחר ב-1947 לחבר החברה המלכותית של לונדון.
claims.quote: Krebs was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of London in 1947.

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, קרבס קיבל פרסים רבים, ובהם פרס לסקר למחקר רפואי בסיסי (1953), המדליה המלכותית (1954) ומדלית קופלי (1961).
claims.quote: Krebs received numerous other awards, including the Albert Lasker Award for Basic Medical Research (1953), Royal Medal of the Royal Society London (1954), Copley Medal (1961)

claims.text: ב-1966 הוכתר קרבס כאזרח כבוד של עיר הולדתו הילדסהיים, לפי הלאופולדינה.
claims.quote: In 1966, Hans Krebs became an honorary citizen of his native city of Hildesheim.

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, ב-2012 נקרא רחוב על שמו של קרבס בפרייבורג.
claims.quote: In addition, a street was named after him in Freiburg in 2012.

claims.text: ב-1954 מונה קרבס לפרופסור ויטלי לביוכימיה באוניברסיטת אוקספורד.
claims.quote: In 1954 he was appointed Whitley Professor of Biochemistry in the University of Oxford

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, כנראה לא היה קל לקרבס להשתלב באוקספורד, לפחות בהתחלה.
claims.quote: Krebs probably found it not too easy to fit into Oxford, at least at first.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, כשקרבס התייעץ עם רודולף פיטרס לפני המעבר לאוקספורד, פיטרס סבר שקרבס אינו האדם האידיאלי לתפקיד.
claims.quote: Peters thought that Krebs was not the ideal person for the post

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, בתקופת אוקספורד התגלה מחזור הגליאוקסילאט, שינוי של מחזור חומצת הלימון.
claims.quote: A major scientific advance made during the Oxford period was the discovery of a new cycle, the glyoxylate cycle, which is a modification of the citric acid cycle

claims.text: ב-1957 פרסם קרבס בשיתוף ה' ל' קורנברג סקירה על טרנספורמציות אנרגיה בחומר חי.
claims.quote: Among his many publications is the remarkable survey of energy transformations in living matter, published in 1957, in collaboration with H. L. Kornberg

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, קרבס מת ב-22 בנובמבר 1981 באוקספורד, ועד סמוך למותו היה פעיל מדעית.
claims.quote: Hans Krebs passed away on 22 November 1981 in Oxford, where he was still scientifically active shortly before his death.

claims.text: לפי JTA, קרבס היה פליט יהודי מגרמניה שהפך לאחד המדענים המובהקים של בריטניה, ומת באוקספורד בגיל 81.
claims.quote: Sir Hans Krebs, a German Jewish refugee who became one of Britain’s most distinguished scientists, has died in Oxford at the age of 81.

claims.text: לפי JTA, קרבס הוזמן לבריטניה לאחר עליית היטלר לשלטון והיה פרופסור לביוכימיה באוניברסיטאות שפילד ואוקספורד.
claims.quote: He was invited to Britain after Hitler came to power and became a professor of biochemistry at Sheffield and Oxford Universities.

claims.text: לפי הקולג' המלכותי לרופאים, קרבס הכשיר מספר רב של ביוכימאים והשפעתו על התפתחות הביוכימיה, בארץ ובעולם, הייתה עמוקה.
claims.quote: his influence on the development of biochemistry both nationally and internationally was profound

claims.text: לפי אוניברסיטת פרייבורג, קרבס היה אחד מהחוקרים הגרמנים-יהודים המעטים שהצליחו להמשיך בקריירה ללא הפרעה לאחר גירושם מגרמניה הנאצית.
claims.quote: Krebs was one of the few German-Jewish scholars who were able to continue their careers without interruption after banishment from Nazi Germany.

claims.text: קרבס נישא ב-1938 למרגרט סיסילי פילדהאוס מוויקרסלי שביורקשייר.
claims.quote: He married Margaret Cicely Fieldhouse, of Wickersley, Yorkshire, in 1938.

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, בנו של קרבס, ג'ון קרבס, הוא פרופסור לזואולוגיה באוקספורד וחבר בבית הלורדים.
claims.quote: His son John Krebs is a zoology professor at Oxford and a member of the House of Lords.

claims.text: לפי המחלקה לביוכימיה בקיימברידג', קרבס פוטר ממשרתו במרפאה הרפואית של אוניברסיטת פרייבורג באפריל 1933.
claims.quote: a post from which he was dismissed in April 1933

claims.text: לפי אוטוביוגרפיית נובל, ביוני 1933 הממשלה הנציונל-סוציאליסטית סיימה את העסקתו של קרבס.
claims.quote: In June 1933, the National Socialist Government terminated his appointment

claims.text: לפי הלאופולדינה, קרבס כבר ברח לאנגליה ב-10 ביוני 1933 בגלל החוק נגד מדענים יהודים.
claims.quote: He had already fled to England on 10 June 1933 for this very reason

claims.text: לפי אותו מקור, הם הראו שמעורב כאן מסלול מחזורי.
claims.quote: They were able to show that a cyclical pathway was involved
